name: GA-08
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+15 district with a long-serving incumbent running for reelection
Scott holds a massive financial edge: $1.35M on hand versus under $2,000 for Esti
Prediction markets price Scott near 95%; no polls or expert ratings flag any risk
model.rationale: Austin Scott's financial dominance and the district's strong Republican lean leave Kelly Esti, who has raised under $20,000, without a visible path; markets and fundamentals alike point to a double-digit Republican win.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a competitive race or a surge of Democratic outside spending would be the main signal of movement, though nothing currently suggests either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 8th District covers rural middle Georgia and leans heavily Republican, with a partisan index roughly fifteen points to the right of the country. Austin Scott has held the seat since 2011 and is running again after securing renomination. His Democratic challenger, Kelly Esti, has run a minimal campaign, reporting about nineteen thousand dollars raised and under two thousand on hand.

Scott, by contrast, has raised over a million dollars and holds more than 1.3 million in cash, with no meaningful outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Scott roughly a ninety-five percent chance of winning. The combination of a deep-red district, a well-funded incumbent, and an opponent with negligible resources points to a comfortable Republican victory in the double digits.
